record.scope: Intermittent obstruction of Iraq-to-Jordan oil consignments on the Trebil approach, ending by completion of affected October deliveries

followup_reviews.Research finding: Fresh Petra/Ammon ministry reports support the recorded 25–27 October selective sequence. Al Hadath’s indexed analyst account adds early-morning activity on 25 October but cannot prove the first-ever onset. Seven observed entries on 26 October and completion of the month’s consignments on 27 October remain different facts; no continuous two-day spell or ordinary-freight restriction is established.

followup_reviews.Root decision: Accept seven new parents, eight phases on those parents and one additional May2024 phase on ME026, plus both targeted unresolved Trebil questions. Apply all65 guarded challenger refinements: urgent exceptions in April2018; August2018 reopening established only by August12, with earliest bound unknown; December2023 commercial-only scope with ordinary passengers unaffected. Retain partial and directional Rafah/plant-fuel scopes, operational versus announced May2024 returns, all unknowns and conflicts, fifteen unresolved issues and nine unlocated phases. No numerical duration is invented from a reported day count or general reopening announcement.
followup_reviews.Issue dispositions: REC50-R13-Q01 — Earliest obstruction, first post-obstruction passage and intraday continuity remain unresolved; location/count wording differs across accounts. Existing unknowns and intermittent coding remain unchanged.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Seven tanker entries on October 26 and the ministry’s October 27 completion of the affected monthly consignments support an intermittent tanker-specific episode and its latest completion bound. They do not establish a whole-border closure, a continuous blockage or exact first reopening.
